title: Uncle Sam Gets Heavy In Brazil
gist: Gavekal expects Brazil may join the US political orbit if Flávio Bolsonaro wins the run-off, but notes US critical minerals investment, especially heavy rare earths, is already surging under Lula.

insights.claim: Flávio Bolsonaro narrowly leads polls ahead of Sunday's presidential run-off, making it likely Brazil follows other right-leaning Latin American nations into the US political orbit.
insights.speaker: Tom Miller
insights.so_what: Election outcome could shift Brazil's alignment and asset risk premia.

insights.claim: Brazil is the leading producer of heavy rare earths outside Asia, and the US is targeting its mines to break China's chokehold.
insights.speaker: Tom Miller
insights.so_what: Brazil rare-earth projects are strategic supply alternatives to China.

insights.claim: A Bolsonaro presidency is not decisive for US critical minerals investment, which is already surging under President Lula; what matters is that the US is gaining China-free supply of heavy rare earths.
insights.speaker: Tom Miller
insights.so_what: The rare-earth theme in Brazil is policy-agnostic; own it regardless of the election outcome.
